Messages.Author: Laura Gabrielle
Messages.Body:
1) Does Dr. Jest's ability (to cause opponent to discard a card at
random) cause him to tap as an action? Or is it just an automatic
thing if he is untapped during the master phase?

2) In the Basic game as outlined in the V:TES mini-rule book, how many
cards can a vamp play in the single round of combat? ie, how many of
each type: combat, reaction, action modifier...

3) An opponent delcares a bleed as an action, if it is not blocked can
he then play an action card to increase the bleed or does he have to
play the action card as the bleed is being declared?

4) An opponent attempts to bleed me with a vamp that has +1 bleed, if
I block this action what type of damage does my blocking minion take,
the bleed damage or the hand/equipment damage? (ie, what's the
difference between hand and bleed damage?) Anothe example would be if
the opponent played an action card to increase the bleed to +3, if I
successfully block this action are we talking hand damage now and the
bleed action card is nullified?

Thanx

Messages.Author: L. Scott Johnson
Messages.Body:
ls...@hq.tcfarm.com (Laura Gabrielle) writes:

>1) Does Dr. Jest's ability (to cause opponent to discard a card at
>random) cause him to tap as an action? Or is it just an automatic
>thing if he is untapped during the master phase?

Automatic. It even applies if Jest is in Torpor (untapped).

>2) In the Basic game as outlined in the V:TES mini-rule book, how many
>cards can a vamp play in the single round of combat? ie, how many of
>each type: combat, reaction, action modifier...

You cannot play reactions nor action modifiers in combat. But there
is no restriction on the number of combat cards (duplicates or no)
that you can play - but you can't maneuver twice in a row, nor prevent
damage that you haven't taken, nor press twice in a row.

>3) An opponent delcares a bleed as an action, if it is not blocked can
>he then play an action card to increase the bleed or does he have to
>play the action card as the bleed is being declared?

After the block is declined is fine. The would-be blocker does not get
the chance to change his mind.

>4) An opponent attempts to bleed me with a vamp that has +1 bleed, if
>I block this action what type of damage does my blocking minion take,
>the bleed damage or the hand/equipment damage? (ie, what's the
>difference between hand and bleed damage?) Anothe example would be if
>the opponent played an action card to increase the bleed to +3, if I
>successfully block this action are we talking hand damage now and the
>bleed action card is nullified?

Bleed and hand damage are completely independent. Increasing one
will not affect the other.

Messages.Author: Stephen Beaulieu
Messages.Body:
In article <4leirt$2...@news.tcfarm.com>, ls...@hq.tcfarm.com wrote:

: 1) Does Dr. Jest's ability (to cause opponent to discard a card at

: random) cause him to tap as an action? Or is it just an automatic
: thing if he is untapped during the master phase?

His ability is automatic during the master phase and requires no tapping
or action on his part.

: 2) In the Basic game as outlined in the V:TES mini-rule book, how many

: cards can a vamp play in the single round of combat? ie, how many of
: each type: combat, reaction, action modifier...

Each minion/vamp can take one action, which taps them. During that action
the acting minion can play one copy of a given action modifier, a given
reacting minion can play one given reaction card. A different reacting
minion could play the another copy of that reaction card.

In combat the only restrictions are: for each strike a minion has, he or
she can only play one strike card; a minion can only use one card a round
that give additional strikes; and that if a strike based card is used to
manuever (a gun, Thrown Gate, Aid with Bats..) that card must be used as
the minion's strike for the round (any additional strikes in that round
can be anything the vamp wants and has the cards for) and therefore only
one strike based card can be used to generate a manuever in a given round
(ie no manuever with the gun and then manuever with a Thrown gate in the
same round.); also each minion must delcare a strike (you cannot choose
not to strike)

Example will follow below.

: 3) An opponent delcares a bleed as an action, if it is not blocked can

: he then play an action card to increase the bleed or does he have to
: play the action card as the bleed is being declared?

A minion cannot play an action card at this point in time, but could play
action modifiers after the block has been not blocked or the targetted
Meth has given up the opportunity to block. A bleeding action card (Like
Govern the Unaligned) has to be declared and played as teh action is
announced. A bleeding action modifier (like Threats) can be played as teh
action is announced, but it is generally better to play when you know the
bleed will be successful.

: 4) An opponent attempts to bleed me with a vamp that has +1 bleed, if

: I block this action what type of damage does my blocking minion take,
: the bleed damage or the hand/equipment damage? (ie, what's the
: difference between hand and bleed damage?) Anothe example would be if
: the opponent played an action card to increase the bleed to +3, if I
: successfully block this action are we talking hand damage now and the
: bleed action card is nullified?

Bleed damage and combat damage are fundamentally different and separate
things. Bleed damage is the number of blood counters removed from the
Meth's pool to the blood bank if the bleeding action is successful (ie,
not blocked or countered.) The amount of potential bleed has nothing to
do with the damage that vampire would deal out in combat. The damage
dealt in the combat depends on the strikes the minions deal out (either
via a gun or whatever.)

Your second example is correct.

Right, now here are two examples that will break down the basic play and
what restrictions there are.

You control Dr. Jest. Your preadator controls Deiter Kleist and Dorian
Strack (with a .44 Magnum and a potence skill card). (I think these vamps
will work. In either case the vamp with the gun should have superior
celerity and normal auspex and potence, the other vamp should have normal
auspex, with the other skill not mattering.)

It is your turn.

Example 1

In your minion phase you decide to bleed with Dr. Jest (no action card.)
Both Deiter and Dorain are untapped. Your prey does not declare a blocker
(thus the action is unblocked) and instead has Deiter play a Telepathic
Counter (reducing the bleed by 1). You decide to play a Conditioning from
your hand to increase the bleed by 3. Your prey has given up the
opportunity to block and cannot choose to block now. But Dorain can play
another Telepathic Counter (as Deiter played the first one) and does so,
reducing the bleed by another point. You are restricted (by card text,
from playing additional bleed modifiers, and therefore the action is
concluded)

End result: you bleed your prey for 2 pool (which your prey burns to the
blood bank) and you get the Edge.

Example 2 (This assumes an advanced game with stealth and intercept. If
you are not at that point yet the rest of the example is still valid and
the stealth/intercept just points out the action modifier restrictions.)

Same situation. You choose to have Dr Jest perform a Govern the Unaligned
action at the inferior (bleed at +2...this action card must be played
now). Dorian declares a block. You play Lost in Crowds to increase your
stealth by 1. Dorian plays an Enhanced Senses to increase intercept by
1. (To block an action you must have as much intercept as the action has
stealth.) You have another Lost in Crowds in your hand, but you cannot
play it because you have already played that action modifier card. You
have no more stealth in your hand so the action is blocked. Dorian taps
and you enter combat. The Govern the Unaligned card is put in the ash
heap and you do not pay for it as the action was unsuccessful.

Combat: (just a reminder the fact that you were bleeding for 3 gived you
no advantage in the combat)

Choose Range
You choose not to Manuever (Dorian has a gun and you want to hit him.)
Dorian manuevers to long range with the gun. You have a Fake Out manuever
card in your hand so you manuever back to close. Dorian has a Thrown Gate
in his hand (Potence card giving a manuever and ranged damage) but he
cannot play it as he used the manuever from the gun to get to long range,
and this commits him to shooting you with the gun as his initial stike of
the round. But he has a Flash in his hand (Celerity at superior a
Manuever with an optional press) and uses it to get to long range. You
have no more manuevers so the combat is at long range.

Strikes
Dr Jest has to choose a strike (so he strikes with hands even though it
will do no damage at long range.)
Dorian has to use the gun as his strike (even though he has the Thrown
Gate and a Thrown Sewer Lid in his hand) He shoots Dr Jest.

Damage Resolution
Dr Jest takes 2 points of damage and removes that pool to the blood bank.

Additional Strikes
Dr Jest has none. Dorian plays a Blur to get 2 additional stikes. (he
cannot play any other cards to get an additional strike) He shoots you for
the first additional strike. Dr Jest takes 2 more points of damage. Then
he Throws a Sewer Lid at Dr Jest. Dr. Jest takes 3 more points of damage
(although he still doesn't go to torpor. I think he is out of blood..
anyway, for arguments sake lets say he is out of blood.)

Presses
Dr Jest doesn't want to continue combat as one more point of damage will
send him to torpor. He does not press. Dorian has an optional press from
the Flash played earlier and uses t. Dr Jest doesn't have any presses so
combat continues.

The same steps are gone through as last round, so I'll shorten them to
just a couple of sentences. Dorian manuevers to long range with teh Thrown
Gate and hits Dr Jest with it for a single point of damage. Dr Jest had
no manuevers or dodges, so goes to torpor in the Damage resolution stage.

End result: Dr Jest gets whooped up on by a small Toreador with potence
and a gun. Moral, make sure you have enough stealth when you can't fight,
or Toreador guns decks can dish it out.. ;^)

I hope these examples have helped to explain how a given action and
corresponding combat might proceed. There are many more examples I might
ahve given. My advice, start playing with the full advanced rules. The
game is so much better than the basic Vtes rules, and not taht much more
difficult to learn. You will enjoy it much more.

i hope this helps

stephen beaulieu
hi...@mail.utexas.edu

Messages.Author: Zach Haffey
Messages.Body:
On Mon, 22 Apr 1996, Laura Gabrielle wrote:

> 1) Does Dr. Jest's ability (to cause opponent to discard a card at
> random) cause him to tap as an action? Or is it just an automatic
> thing if he is untapped during the master phase?

He doesn't tap to do this. Special abilities on the Vamps themselves
would specify to tap.

> 2) In the Basic game as outlined in the V:TES mini-rule book, how many
> cards can a vamp play in the single round of combat? ie, how many of
> each type: combat, reaction, action modifier...
>

You can play as many combat cards as you like and they can be identical.
For example two aura readings can be played, one being used at superior
and one at regular. There are a few restrictions as far as the rules go
though, only one additional strike card can be played in a round (ie no
acrobatics and then blur)

As far as reaction and action modifiers go, you can play as many as you
want as long as they're not the same card (cant use lost in crowds twice
on same action).

> 3) An opponent delcares a bleed as an action, if it is not blocked can
> he then play an action card to increase the bleed or does he have to
> play the action card as the bleed is being declared?

No. You can't attempt a straight bleed and then throw a Govern the
Unaligned or Social charm, Legal Manip, etc on it after they let it
through. These are all action cards and have to be played as you tap the
vamp. Bonding, Threats, Conditioning, Aire of Elation, etc can be played
after it is let through, however, because they are action modifiers and
not actions themselves.

> 4) An opponent attempts to bleed me with a vamp that has +1 bleed, if
> I block this action what type of damage does my blocking minion take,
> the bleed damage or the hand/equipment damage? (ie, what's the
> difference between hand and bleed damage?) Anothe example would be if
> the opponent played an action card to increase the bleed to +3, if I
> successfully block this action are we talking hand damage now and the
> bleed action card is nullified?

ACtually, a vampire's current bleed has nothing to do with how much damage
they do in combat. The default hand damage for a vampire is one unless
you increase it with combat cards, equipment, etc.

(We are going by full game rules and not those weird basic ones, right?)

Hope this helps,
Zach Haffey

> >2) In the Basic game as outlined in the V:TES mini-rule book, how many

Does he mean an action modifier or an action. An action card (such as
legal manipulations) must be played as the action is declared, before
blocking. Action modifiers (like bonding, conditioning etc.) can be
played after the prey declines to block and there's nothing he can do
about it.

Uh...no.

> You may play an ACTION card (i.e. Govern the Unaligned)
> AFTER declaring a bleed action (originally with no card)?
>
> am I reading this wrong or would you need to declare the Gov. unaligned
> as the action?
>

You MUST play the action card (gov. unaligned) as you tap the vampire that's
bleeding. These cards have the two solid black triangles. Action
modifiers (Threats, Bonding, Conditioning, Aire of Elation) are the ones
that go on after the bleed gets through.

-Zach
